title: 3dHome house profile
description:
Schema for a 3dHome house profile. A profile is a directory (houses/<id>/) containing two files:

  geometry.json — the physical model of the house (rooms, walls, doors, lights, materials, coordinate transform). Shareable: it describes shapes, not accounts.
  rooms.json    — the Home Assistant entity binding (room id -> entity ids) and HA connection defaults. Personal: it names your devices.

The split is deliberate. Geometry can be published, forked and diffed; the entity map is an inventory of what is installed in someone's home and belongs in runtime config, never in a public repo. Both files validate against this one schema: pick the branch with the `kind` discriminator ('geometry' or 'rooms').

JOIN KEY: `room id`. Every room in geometry.rooms is keyed by a stable, lowercase, snake_case id. That id — NOT the display label — is what doors reference (door.room), what lights reference (light.room), what rooms.json binds entities to, what the overlays label, and what the engine uses for its per-room lookups. Renaming a room's `label` is free; renaming its id breaks every reference to it. Choose ids once and keep them.

UNITS: see the `units` field on geometry. The profile is authored in CENTIMETRES in the plan's own coordinate space (the same numbers a Sweet Home 3D export produces), and the engine converts to metres at render time via `coordinateTransform`. Heights and thicknesses are also centimetres, for one consistent unit throughout the file. See docs/house-profile.md.

roomId.title: Room id — the stable join key
roomId.description: The identity of a room across every file in the project. Referenced by door.room, light.room, rooms.json's `rooms` map, the debug overlays and the engine's per-room state. Stable forever: change `label` for display, never this. Lowercase letters, digits and underscores only.

entityId.description: A Home Assistant entity id, e.g. "light.demo_kitchen_ceiling" or "binary_sensor.demo_hall_motion". The domain prefix is what tells the engine how to read the state: a `light.*` is switched and dimmed, while a `binary_sensor.*` is read as on/off only.

hexColor.description: An sRGB colour as a CSS hex string, e.g. "#ece9e1". Authored as a string (not a JS 0x number) so the file stays valid JSON and is greppable/diffable.

point2d.description: A point in plan coordinates, [x, y], in the profile's unit (centimetres). x increases EAST, y increases SOUTH — the Sweet Home 3D convention, kept so exported numbers can be used verbatim.

texture.title: A texture image reference
texture.description: Path is resolved RELATIVE TO THE HOUSE PROFILE DIRECTORY (houses/<id>/), never to the page or to src/. So "textures/monstera.png" means houses/<id>/textures/monstera.png. This keeps a profile self-contained and copy-pasteable: a house directory plus its textures is the whole unit. Absolute URLs and paths escaping the profile dir ('..') are rejected — a profile must not be able to point the engine at arbitrary hosts.

path.description: Relative path from the house profile directory to the image file.

fit.description: How the image maps onto the surface. 'stretch' maps one copy of the image across the whole target face (a mural — one continuous picture). 'tile' repeats it (a pattern), using `repeatMetres`.

repeatMetres.description: Only meaningful when fit='tile': real-world size, in metres, that one copy of the image covers. E.g. 1.2 = one copy per 1.2 m.

credit.description: Optional attribution/licence note for the image. Fill this in for a public profile — a shared house profile carrying an unlicensed photo is a licensing problem.

coordinateTransform.title: Plan-space to world-space transform — PER HOUSE, never a constant
coordinateTransform.description:
Maps this house's plan coordinates onto the renderer's world axes. It MUST live in the profile: every Sweet Home 3D export has its own arbitrary origin (wherever the author happened to start drawing), so hardcoding one house's offsets in the engine makes every other house render off-centre or off-scale. The engine applies:

    worldX = (planX - originX) * scale
    worldZ = (planY - originY) * scale

with world +X = East and world +Z = South. `scale` converts the profile's unit to metres. Derive originX/originY by picking any convenient point in your plan (a corner of the building, or the plan's own bounding-box centre) — the choice only shifts where the model sits around the world origin, which matters for camera framing and for the ground/sky rig.

originX.description: Plan-space x that becomes world x = 0.

originY.description: Plan-space y that becomes world z = 0.

scale.description: Multiplier from the profile's unit to metres. For centimetre-authored profiles this is 0.01.

planAxes.description: Documents which compass directions the plan's +x/+y point at, so a plan exported with a different convention can be recognised rather than silently rendered mirrored. Only 'x_east_y_south' is supported today; the field exists so a future importer can detect and convert the others instead of guessing.

label.description: Human-readable name shown in tooltips and the controls panel, e.g. "Living Room". Free to change at any time; it is never a join key.

polygon.description: The room's floor outline as an ordered ring of plan-space points. Do NOT repeat the first point at the end — the ring closes implicitly. Non-rectangular rooms (L-shapes, notches around pillars) are expressed here directly; this is why the format is a polygon rather than a bounding rectangle. The engine derives the room's bounding box, centroid and area from this.

areaSqm.description: OPTIONAL declared floor area in m². Omit it and the engine computes the area from `polygon` by the shoelace formula — that is the recommended default, because a hand-typed area silently goes stale the moment the polygon moves. Supply it only when the authoritative figure differs from the polygon (e.g. a surveyed/legal area that excludes a chimney breast the polygon includes); the engine then displays yours and may warn if the two disagree by more than a few percent.

floorColor.description: Base floor colour for this room, used as a tint under the floor material and as the fallback when no texture loads.

floorMaterial.description: Which built-in procedural floor treatment the engine generates for this room. 'tile' and 'wood' are canvas-generated at runtime (no image file needed); 'carpet' is a noise-based pile. 'none' draws no visible floor for this room (useful when a single house-wide slab already covers it).

rug.description: An optional rug laid on top of the floor. Its outline is independent of the room polygon on purpose: a rug typically laps over pillars and stops short of doorways, so it is neither the room shape nor a plain rectangle.

polygon.description: Rug outline in plan coordinates. Omit to lay a rug over the room's own bounding box inset by `inset`.

inset.description: When `polygon` is absent: shrink the room's bounding box by this many centimetres on every side to get the rug. Use 0 for a floor covering that reaches the walls — a fitted carpet rather than a rug laid inside the room. The default of 30 is a rug-shaped guess and is wrong for a carpeted room, so set it explicitly whenever the covering meets the skirting.

color.description:
The colour the rug should RENDER as. The engine divides it through by its own pile texture before use, so what you write is what you get -- you do not need to know what the pile looks like.

One limit: a texture cannot be brightened past its own values, so a colour lighter than the pile's grey clamps to the pile. Real rugs are darker than that; for a genuinely pale rug supply a pale `texture` instead.

Defaults to white, which renders as the pile's own tone.

pattern.description: A procedural rug look (src/rug-pattern.js, signed off on the Rug spec page): bold zig-zag bands in a palette plus shaggy pile noise, drawn once over the whole rug. Store only what differs from the defaults -- every key is optional and falls back to RUG_PATTERN_DEFAULTS, so `{}` is the default grey/cream/teal chevron shag. The rug's size is NOT a pattern key: it comes from the outline's bounding box, and the pattern's width (the axis the zig-zag spans) follows the rug's long side -- or its short side with `across: "short"` -- whichever plan axis that is. Supersedes `color`, and takes precedence over `texture` if both are given.
'chevron' (default) or 'solid' (the first colour only, still with pile noise).

colors.description: Band colours, cycled in order. Default ["#9a9a96", "#e8e2d4", "#2f7e8c"].

bandWidth.description: Centimetres measured across one band. Default 26.

angle.description: Degrees: the zig-zag's slope off the rug's width axis. Default 40.

zigzags.description: Full zig-zags across the rug's width (long side). Default 1: one big V.

pileNoise.description: 0 = a flat print; about 0.2 = shag (fuzzed band edges, shaded strands). Default 0.18.

seed.description: Seed for the pile noise, so the same rug always looks the same. Default 1.

across.description: Which side of the rug the zig-zag spans: 'long' (default, as on the Rug spec page) or 'short'. With 'short' the bands stack down the rug's length, so the chevrons march along the long side. Measure it off the real rug: on a 'long' rug one V is as wide as the rug is long.

notes.description: Why this rug's outline is what it is. Worth filling in: a rug polygon almost always differs from the room polygon for a physical reason (it laps over a pillar, it stops short of a doorway), and without the note the next editor 'corrects' it back to the room shape.

footstepZone.title: Manual footstep-trail confinement
footstepZone.description:
OPTIONAL override for where the presence footstep trail walks in this room. Absent (the default for every room today): the engine derives placement automatically from the room polygon and its doors -- the door with the longest clear run decides the start point and direction, and the walk turns once around an L-shaped corner. That automatic placement can still look wrong for a real, furnished room the polygon alone does not describe (a counter run, a dining table, a doorway that leads toward a smaller side room), which is exactly what this field is for: a rectangle, in the room's own coordinates, that the walk is confined to instead of the full polygon.

COORDINATES ARE RELATIVE TO THE ROOM'S BOUNDING-BOX MIN CORNER (x1,y1), not absolute plan coordinates -- so a zone survives the room polygon being nudged during authoring, and so it can be written by looking at the room in isolation without re-deriving the house's global origin. The engine adds the room's derived bbox min corner back on before using it.

This is a STARTING value for the room owner to tune by eye against the rendered result, not a computed placement -- unlike everything else the loader derives, nobody can get this right on the first guess from measurements alone.

from.description: One corner of the confinement rectangle, in centimetres relative to the room's bbox min corner. Paired with `to`; the engine sorts them, so `from` need not be the top-left corner.

to.description: The opposite corner of the confinement rectangle, same coordinate space as `from`.

relativeTo.description: Named explicitly (rather than left implicit) so a future zone anchored some other way -- to a fixture, say -- cannot be confused with this one by an engine version that predates it. Today "room" (the bbox min corner) is the only value the engine understands; anything else is ignored with a warning and the room falls back to automatic placement, the same 'absent' behaviour as when the field is omitted entirely.

footstepPath.title: Authored footstep route
footstepPath.description:
OPTIONAL route for the presence footstep trail in this room: an ordered list of waypoints the trail walks along, first to last. Waypoint order IS the direction of travel -- prints are laid from the first waypoint to the last (both ends get a print), evenly spaced at the stride nearest the engine's default that fits the path, alternating left and right of the line and facing along it. Use this when the owner knows the route people actually take (under a table, along a corridor to a radiator) and neither automatic placement nor a footstepZone rectangle can express it. TAKES PRECEDENCE over footstepZone; absent, the room behaves exactly as before.

COORDINATES ARE RELATIVE TO THE ROOM'S BOUNDING-BOX MIN CORNER (x1,y1), the same convention as footstepZone. Every waypoint must lie inside the room polygon; a path with any waypoint outside it is ignored with a warning and the room falls back to footstepZone or automatic placement.

Regardless of the path, no print is ever laid within the engine's door gap (40cm, measured from the print's centre) of any door opening -- so start and end the path a little way clear of doorways, or the prints nearest the door are simply not drawn.

points.description: Waypoints in walking order, in centimetres relative to the room's bbox min corner. At least two.

relativeTo.description: As footstepZone.relativeTo: named explicitly so a future anchoring cannot be mistaken for this one. "room" (the bbox min corner) is the only value the engine understands; anything else is ignored with a warning.

smooth.description: Round the corners between waypoints so the trail curves rather than turning on the spot. Endpoints are never moved. Set false for a deliberately sharp turn.

notes.description: Why the route goes where it does (e.g. 'under the table, not around it'). Never rendered.
Free-text note for whoever edits this profile next. Never rendered.

wall.title: A wall segment
wall.description:
One straight run of wall, given by its CENTRELINE endpoints in plan coordinates plus a thickness. Interior and exterior walls are the SAME shape of record — they differ only by the `exterior` flag, which controls fade-away behaviour when the camera looks into the house from outside. (The reference implementation this schema was derived from kept a single WALLS array with an `outer: 0|1` field and derived its exterior set from that; keeping one list avoids the class of bug where a wall is edited in one array and not the other.)

Pillars and stub returns are ordinary walls: a short segment with a large thickness.

id.description: Permanent wall number. This is what a human says out loud ("wall 22 has the wallpaper") and what the wall-debug overlay prints, so it must NOT be derived from array position: deleting a wall would then silently renumber every later one. Retire an id when its wall is removed and never reuse it; mint new ids above `walls.highestIdEverAssigned`.

thickness.description: Wall thickness in centimetres, measured perpendicular to the centreline. Defaults to `defaults.wallThickness` when omitted.

exterior.description: true = part of the building's outer shell. Exterior walls participate in the camera-facing fade so you can see inside; interior walls stay solid. Note this is a RENDERING role, not a structural claim — a pillar in the middle of a room may be marked exterior purely to make it fade with the shell behind it, or interior to keep it always solid.

height.description: Wall height in centimetres. Defaults to `defaults.wallHeight`. Override for a half-height partition or a parapet.

faceTexture.description: Applies wallpaper / a mural to ONE face of this wall. Which face is named by `side`.

side.description: Which face of the wall carries the texture, as a compass direction. The engine resolves this against the wall's own orientation, so you name the side the way you would in the room ('the north face'), not in the renderer's local axes.

clipToRoom.description: Optional: paper only the portion of this wall face that borders the named room. A long wall often runs past several rooms while the wallpaper covers only one of them; without this the image stretches across the whole run.

finishes.description: OPTIONAL per-face finishes: brick, tile... on ONE long face of this wall each, optionally over only a height range and a span along the wall. The finish is drawn procedurally (no image file) at its real size, and fades with its wall. A finish covering a face completely costs no extra mesh; a partial one is a thin panel over just that rectangle, and skips the wall's doors and windows. Added in schemaVersion 1.3; an older engine ignores it.

wallFinish.title: A finish on one face of a wall
wallFinish.description: Names ONE long face of the wall -- by `side` ("exterior", or a compass side) or by `room` (the face that fronts that room, derived exactly as a window's room face is) -- and puts `finish` on it. Give exactly one of `side` and `room`. `from`/`to` limit it to a height band and `along` to a span of the wall; omit them to cover the whole face.

finish.description: `brick`: the running-bond buff brick the WindowSpec and BalconyWindowSpec pages draw on the outer leaf (UK 215 x 65 mm brick, 10 mm joint). `tile`: the bathroom spec pages' tile -- a 40 x 25 cm landscape tile in a 0.4 cm grout joint, greige face, darker grout, flat by default; `look` changes any of that.

side.description: `exterior`: the long face pointing away from the house footprint's centre (judged per wall -- name a compass side instead for a wall in the notch of an L-shaped house). A compass side names the face that looks that way: a LONG face (north/south of an east-west wall, east/west of a north-south one) or an END face (north/south of a north-south wall -- e.g. the north face of a pillar authored as a short north-south segment). `start`/`end`: the end face at the segment's authored start or end point.

room.description: The face of this wall that fronts this room. The room must actually border the wall (over `along`, if given).

from.description: Bottom of the finish, cm above the floor. Omit to start at the bottom of the wall (below the floor, for an exterior wall that runs down through the slab).

to.description: Top of the finish, cm above the floor -- e.g. tiles stopping below the ceiling. Omit to run to the top of the wall. Must be above `from`.

along.description: [start, end]: the span of the wall to finish, in plan cm on the wall's long axis (x for an east-west wall, y for a north-south one) -- the same convention as `door.centre`. Omit to finish the whole length. Needs an axis-aligned wall; ignored on an end face.

look.title: How a tile finish looks
look.description: Tile only (ignored, with a warning, on brick). Every property is optional and defaults to the bathroom spec pages' flat tile. A bad value is warned about and falls back to its default; the tile is still drawn.

size.description: [width, height] of one tile in cm, grout included (the pitch). Default [40, 25].

grout.description: The joint between tiles, cm. Default 0.4. 0 = butt-jointed.

relief.description: 0 (default) = a flat tile. Otherwise each tile's face is embossed with a grid of squares about this many cm across, each its own shade, with a faint highlight between them (not grout) -- 5 on a 40 x 25 tile is the spec's 8 x 5 wet-area tile.

roughness.description: The material's roughness. Default 0.55; the spec's wet-area tile is 0.35.

reveals.description: Also wrap the finish round the reveals (jambs) of the wall's doors and windows and round the wall's own ends, within the finish's height band -- as brick returns into a window opening. Defaults to true for `side: "exterior"` and false otherwise.

door.title: A door
door.description:
A door is an opening in a wall plus a swinging leaf. Position is given the way a floor plan gives it — 'in this wall, this far along, this wide' — rather than as a free-floating 3D transform, so it stays attached when the wall moves.

HINGE AND SWING ARE SEPARATE AND BOTH REQUIRED. `hinge` says which END of the opening the leaf is attached to; `swing` says which SIDE of the wall it opens into. Those are independent: the same hinge end with the opposite swing gives a door that opens the other way, which is what makes it hit a cupboard instead of clearing it. Both are compass directions, so they can be read straight off an annotated plan.

id.description: Stable identifier for this door, e.g. "front_door". Used by the door-debug overlay and by anything that animates a specific door.

wall.description: The `id` of the wall this door sits in. Referencing the wall by id (rather than re-stating the wall's coordinate) means moving a wall carries its doors with it, and a door in a deleted wall is a detectable error rather than a door floating in space.

centre.description: Position of the opening's centre along the wall, in centimetres, measured in plan coordinates on the wall's own long axis (x for an east-west wall, y for a north-south wall). This is the number a plan gives you directly.

width.description: Leaf width in centimetres (the clear opening, excluding the frame reveal).

height.description: Leaf height in centimetres. Defaults to `defaults.doorHeight`.

hinge.description: Which END of the opening carries the hinges, as a compass direction. For an east-west wall use 'east' or 'west'; for a north-south wall use 'north' or 'south'. Getting this wrong mirrors the door about its centre.

swing.description: Which SIDE of the wall the leaf opens into, as a compass direction — i.e. which room it swings into. Must be perpendicular to `hinge`: an east-west wall hinges east/west and swings north/south, and vice versa. A validator should reject a parallel pair, because it is always an authoring mistake and renders as a leaf embedded in its own wall.

maxOpenDegrees.description: How far this door can open, in degrees — PER DOOR, because doors genuinely differ: a front or internal room door swings ~90°, while a small cupboard or utility door is stopped by an adjacent wall or its own return at roughly 25–30°. This is the *intended* maximum; the engine may reduce it further at load time if two open leaves would collide, but it will never raise it above this value. Set it from the real door, not from a category default.

kind.description: What sort of door this is. Purely descriptive — it does NOT set the open angle (that is `maxOpenDegrees`, always explicit) — but it lets the engine style the leaf (a front door gets an exterior finish) and lets a collision solver decide who yields: when two leaves clash, a 'standard' door gives way before a 'cupboard' one.

room.description: The room this door BELONGS TO for control purposes — the room whose door-open slider drives it. Usually the room it opens into. A door between two rooms belongs to exactly one of them; pick the one a person would name when asked 'which room's door is this?'. Must be an id present in `rooms`.

restOpenFraction.description: How far open this door sits by default, as a fraction of its solved maximum. 0 = closed, 1 = fully open. Setting this is a deliberate statement about a real door (a permanently-propped archway) and overrides everything: the door rests here whether or not a sensor is bound to it. Omit it and the door rests closed unless a contact sensor is bound in rooms.json, in which case it rests at `defaults.doorRestOpenFraction` until the first reading arrives.

color.description: Leaf colour. Defaults to `materials.doorSlabColor`. Set per-door for a front door in a different finish from the internal ones.

window.title: A window or a balcony glazing run
window.description:
An opening carved through a wall plus a glazed assembly, positioned exactly like a door: `wall` id + `centre` along it, so it follows the wall when the wall moves.

Which face of the wall is the room's is DERIVED from `room` (the side of the wall's centreline the room lies on), so there is no inside/outside field to contradict it.

The frame sits flush with the host wall's OUTER face and reaches into the wall; the room side of the wall shows a plain reveal. For a cavity wall modelled as two parallel segments (an inner and an outer leaf), put the frame's leaf in `wall` and the other leaf in `throughWalls`: the opening is cut through both and the cill spans the whole sandwich.

Two kinds, after the two spec pages:
  window  — WindowSpec (Pivot window): a fixed lower pane under a centre-pivot upper sash, split by a transom at `topSplit`.
  balcony — the Balcony window on WindowSpec: a wide fixed pane beside a hinged glass door that swings OUTWARD, the door at the `doorSide` end.

Added in schemaVersion 1.1.

label.description: Display name. Defaults to the id.

kind.description: `window` = fixed lower pane + centre-pivot upper sash (WindowSpec). `balcony` = fixed pane + hinged outward-swinging glass door (WindowSpec, Balcony window).

room.description: The room the window belongs to. Also decides which face of the wall is the inside.

wall.description: The `id` of the wall the frame sits in. Must run along plan x or plan y.

throughWalls.description: OPTIONAL further wall ids the opening is cut through — the other leaf (or leaves) of a cavity wall modelled as parallel segments. Each must run parallel to `wall`.

centre.description: Centre of the opening along the wall, in plan centimetres on the wall's long axis — the same convention as `door.centre`.

width.description: Glazed width in centimetres. The frame adds a 4 cm reveal each side, and the wall is carved to that.

height.description: Glazed height in centimetres, measured UP FROM `sill` (so the top of the glass is at sill + height, the Sweet Home 3D elevation + height convention).

sill.description: Height of the bottom of the glazing above the floor, in centimetres. A floor-level window with a small step-over cill is a few centimetres. Values under 4 are raised to 4, the depth of the frame's bottom member.

topSplit.description: `window` only: the fraction of the glazed height taken by the openable top sash.

doorSide.description: `balcony` only: which END of the glazing run the hinged door is at (and hinged on). Must lie along the wall — east/west for an east-west wall, north/south for a north-south one. Defaults to west (or south).

doorFraction.description: `balcony` only: the fraction of the run's width taken by the door.

frameColor.description: Frame and sash colour. Defaults to an off-white uPVC.

curtain.title: A curtain pair (blackout or sheer)
curtain.description:
A CurtainSpec curtain: floor-to-ceiling, centre-parted into a left and a right half, two-tone pinch-pleat, under a white cornice with a strip light. Hung on the ROOM face of a wall and positioned like a door and a window: `wall` id + `centre` along it. Which face is the room's is derived from `room`.

A SHEER is the same curtain with `opacity` below 1: one translucent layer with no lining. Hang it behind (window side of) a blackout on the same wall by giving it a smaller `offset` and `cornice.enabled: false`; curtains sharing a wall are stacked automatically so their folds never pass through each other.

Every colour is a field here rather than a constant in the engine, because colours are what an owner most wants to change. For a single-colour curtain set `outerColor` and `innerColor` to the same value.

The pose is static: `openPct` says how it hangs. There is no animation and no Home Assistant binding yet.

Added in schemaVersion 1.1.

centre.description: Centre along the wall, plan centimetres — usually the window's own centre.

width.description: Closed width in centimetres: the span of the pair when drawn.

top.description: Height the fabric hangs from, in centimetres above the floor. Defaults to the ceiling height (floor-to-ceiling).

height.description: Drop in centimetres, measured down from `top`. Defaults to `top` (reaches the floor).

openPct.description: How open it hangs: 0 = drawn closed across the window, 100 = gathered into a stack at each end.

stackWidth.description: Width of the gathered stack at EACH end when fully open (100%), in centimetres per side. Measure it on the real curtain: how much wall one half still covers when drawn right back. Overrides `stackPerPleat`. Omit both and the stack is 4.7 cm per pleat (outerPleats + innerPleats per half). Never wider than a closed half. The same value drives the fabric and how much daylight the open curtain still blocks.

stackPerPleat.description: Centimetres of fully-open stack per pleat, per side: the stack is this x (outerPleats + innerPleats). For a fabric that bunches thicker or thinner than the 4.7 cm default. Ignored when `stackWidth` is given.

opacity.description: 1 = an opaque (blackout) curtain with a lining. Below 1 = a SHEER: a single translucent layer at this opacity, e.g. 0.4.

offset.description: Distance of the hanging line from the wall's room face, in centimetres. Defaults to half the cornice depth (CurtainSpec hangs from the cornice's mid-line), or 9 with no cornice. The folds swing either side of this line.

outerColor.description: Colour of the OUTER pleats of each half (from the wall end inward). Default pink #d98aa8.

innerColor.description: Colour of the INNER pleats of each half (toward the centre part). Default blue #5f86c4.

outerPleats.description: Number of outer-colour pleats per half.

innerPleats.description: Number of inner-colour pleats per half. outerPleats + innerPleats must be at least 2.

liningColor.description: Tint of the window-facing lining (opaque curtains only). Default #e7dcc4.

cornice.description: The pelmet box the curtain hangs under. Solid white by default, with a warm strip light along its inside. Set `enabled: false` for a curtain that hangs under another curtain's cornice (a sheer behind a blackout).

sideFaces.description: true: a box just wider than the curtain, closed back to the wall at each end. false: a wall-to-wall front face spanning the whole room, with no ends.

height.description: Front-face height, cm, hanging down from `top`.

light.description: Draw the glowing strip light inside the front face. On the mid and ultra quality tiers it also throws light: a row of downlights (3, or 5 on a cornice 250 cm or wider) shining out of the cornice's open bottom onto the curtain heading and the wall.

furnitureItem.title: A piece of furniture
furnitureItem.description:
One placed item. Two anchor forms; an item uses exactly one.

FREE: `at` [x, y] is the CENTRE of the footprint in plan cm, and `rotation` is degrees CLOCKWISE in plan (y points south). 0 = the front faces +y (south); 90 west, 180 north, 270 east. The front direction is (-sin r, cos r). This is Sweet Home 3D's x/y/angle convention verbatim.

WALL: `wall` + `centre` + `offset`. The item's BACK sits `offset` cm off the ROOM face of `wall`, centred at `centre` along it, and its front faces into `room`. Which face is the room's is derived exactly as for windows and curtains. `rotation` must not be given.

`params` are the builder's own options (see each type's `furnitureParams_<type>` block); anything omitted falls back to the builder's DEFAULTS. An unknown or not-yet-built `type` is skipped with a warning.

Added in schemaVersion 1.2.

room.description: The room the item stands in. For a wall anchor it also decides which face of the wall is the front side.

type.description: The builder, as named in src/furniture/registry.js.

at.description: FREE anchor: footprint centre, plan cm.

rotation.description: FREE anchor only: degrees clockwise in plan; 0 = front faces south (+y).

wall.description: WALL anchor: the host wall's id. Must run along plan x or plan y.

centre.description: WALL anchor: the back's centre, as a coordinate along the wall (x for an east-west wall, y for a north-south one). Must lie within the wall's span.

offset.description: WALL anchor: gap between the wall's room face and the item's back, cm.

elevation.description: Floor to the bottom of the item, cm. Wall-mounted items use this.

params.description: The builder's options. Checked per type against `$defs/furnitureParams_<type>`.

priority.description: `minor` items are dropped on the low GPU tier.

source.description: Where the item came from (e.g. {"sh3d": "<piece name>"}). Documentation only.

furnitureFade.description: How the item fades when the camera looks in through a wall. "auto" (default): items taller than 100 cm fade with their exterior host wall, or a free item with the nearest exterior wall it stands against. "never": always drawn. {"wall": <id>}: fade with that exterior wall.

furnitureParams_balcony.description: Params for `balcony` (src/furniture/balcony.js): a cantilevered balcony -- a slab plus a balustrade of vertical metal bars or glass panels. The BACK (z = 0) is the building face, `width` runs along the facade and the front railing runs along z = depth. The envelope is ALWAYS width x depth x height (slab bottom to rail top). Left and right are as seen from the FRONT, looking at the building (+x is right). The clear gap between adjacent vertical members is held at or below 10 cm at full detail whatever barSpacing says. Each `default` equals balcony.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm, along the facade (the slab's length and the front railing's run).

depth.description: cm, building face to the front of the railing.

height.description: cm, slab bottom to the top of the rail.

slabThickness.description: cm, the slab's thickness (y 0 .. slabThickness). Clamped to at most half the height.

railingThickness.description: cm, the top rail and post section. Clamped to a quarter of the smaller of width and depth.

railing.description: `bars` = top rail, bottom rail and vertical metal bars; `glass` = top rail and glass panels between posts.

barSpacing.description: cm, the target CENTRE spacing of the bars. The clear gap between bars is held at or below 10 cm (and at least 1 cm) regardless.

leftSide.description: The end at x = -width/2 (left as seen from the front): the same balustrade back to the building face, a solid panel, or open.

rightSide.description: The end at x = +width/2 (right as seen from the front).

glassColor.description: Glass panels (glass finish, drawn on their own).

furnitureParams_bathtub.description: Params for `bathtub` (src/furniture/bathroom.js, TYPES['bathtub']): a straight built-in bath (lofted curved ceramic shell, rolled deck, deep rounded inner basin, chrome waste). `width` is the run along the wall. Each `default` equals bathroom.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs). Generic, illustrative defaults; a real room's values live in its furniture[].params.

width.description: cm, along the wall / the item's local x.

height.description: cm, bottom to top.

rim.description: cm, the flat deck around the inner basin.

wasteEnd.description: which end the plug is at, as you face the bath.

furnitureParams_bed.description: Params for `bed` (src/furniture/bed.js): a soft upholstered bed, made up -- vertical padded channels inside a padded border on the headboard, upholstered side and foot rails on a dark recessed plinth, a rounded crowned mattress in a fitted sheet, a draped duvet with a folded-back top edge, sleeping pillows, propped accent pillows and a cushion. Each `default` equals bed.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs). `height` IS the headboard height (floor to its top) -- there is no separate headboardHeight param.

width.description: cm, the frame's outside width (rails and headboard).

depth.description: cm, the frame's outside depth, headboard back to foot rail.

height.description: cm, floor to the top of the headboard -- honoured directly.

baseHeight.description: cm, floor to the top of the upholstered rails. The mattress sits down inside them.

channelCount.description: Vertical padded channels across the headboard, inside its padded border.

channelDepth.description: cm, how far each channel stands proud of the headboard backing at its centre.

baseColor.description: The upholstered rails; the same velvet as the headboard by default.

plinthColor.description: The recessed plinth under the rails.

mattressColor.description: The fitted sheet on the mattress.

accentPillowColor.description: Accent pillows propped against the headboard (full detail).

cushionColor.description: The cushion in the middle (full detail).

duvet.description: Whether the duvet is drawn (draped over the foot end, top edge folded back).

beddingPreset.description: 'botanical' scatters a leaf-and-flower print over the duvet cover (full detail, drawn as geometry); 'plain' leaves it plain.

furnitureParams_box.description: Params for `box` (src/furniture/box.js): a plain box, the test and demo stub and a type for minor clutter. Each `default` equals box.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm, along the wall / the item's local x.

height.description: cm, floor (or `elevation`) to top.

furnitureParams_cabinet.description: Params for `cabinet` (src/furniture/cabinet.js): one configurable cabinet carcass covering wardrobes, display cabinets, a TV console, a chest of drawers, bedside tables, a mobile pedestal and open shelving units. Each `default` equals cabinet.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs). Real params live in a house's furniture[].params; the DEFAULT shown here is a 2-door mirrored wardrobe. See cabinet.js's header comment for the full fronts/columns/glassSidePanel contract - the validator cannot run JavaScript, so this schema only shapes the params, it does not re-derive the builder's fill/normalise/error rules for a fronts row, a columns width, or a glassSidePanel band.

width.description: cm, along the wall / the item's local x.

height.description: cm, floor (or `elevation`) to top, INCLUDING the plinth/legs/wheels.

fronts.description: Row-based front, top to bottom: { height, cells: [ {kind, width, ...} ] }, or a light-channel row { height, channel: { color } } with no cells. Each row's cells must span the cabinet's width, and a row's own height is the space it takes ABOVE the plinth (rows sum to height - plinth.height). Cell kind is one of door|drawer|glass|mirror|sliding|open|stack. Mutually exclusive with `columns` - if both are set, `columns` wins.

channel.description: Makes this row a recessed light channel (the LED bedside tables): no front, set back 1.5 cm, wrapping the front and both sides (not the back), with an emissive strip in `color`. The front directly below gets a glow band along its top edge. Each channel has its own colour, so a later placement can bind each to its own light.

led.description: false: the recess only, with no emissive strip and no glow band.

light.description: The room light channel this level follows (e.g. "bedside_north_top"): its strip and the glow band on the drawer below become live parts posed from that channel's state -- the strip in the light's colour when on and hidden when off, the band washing the drawer front by brightness. Draw the level's real light as a room light strip fixture on the same channel with `drawn: false` (docs/house-profile.md, "Bedside table LED strips").

cells.description: Only for kind:'stack' - this column's own vertical sub-stack of ordinary cells (not itself nesting a stack), { kind, height, ... }, heights summing to the parent row's height.

interior.description: Only for kind:'glass' - the display section behind the glass: `lining` (hex: back, inner walls and ceiling; the floor stays the carcass colour), `shelves` (cm above the section floor, clear glass), `ledStrip` ({ color }: a vertical emissive strip at the back corner on the divider side) and `contents` (low-poly display proxies, full detail only).

columns.description: Column-based front for open shelving, left to right: { width, rows }, `rows` a shelf-row COUNT splitting the column's own clear height into that many equal open bays. Mutually exclusive with `fronts` - if both are set, `columns` wins. null (the default) means this cabinet uses `fronts` instead.

panelThickness.description: cm, carcass panel thickness in `columns` mode only (fronts mode uses a fixed thickness).

inset.description: plinth only: cm the plinth is set back from the fronts' face and from each side (a shadow recess). Omitted: the original 3 cm side inset, centred in the depth (overlay fronts default to 3 cm behind the face).

gloss.description: Carcass/front finish: gloss instead of matte. Ignored when `finish` is set.

finish.description: Carcass, doors, drawers, plinth and shelves: matte, satin or gloss. null (the default) follows `gloss`.

overlayFronts.description: true: the fronts cover the carcass edges (overlay doors) - every carcass and base part ends behind them and each front reaches the carcass outline, so no top or side stands proud of the doors. false: the carcass runs to `depth` with the fronts inside it.

shelfLights.description: Emissive LED strip under a glass shelf front.

handles.description: false = push-to-open, no handle meshes anywhere on this cabinet (a per-cell `handle:false` also works for just one door/drawer).

glassSidePanel.description: Optional override for ONE carcass side (the tall display cabinet): { side: 'left'|'right', bands: [{height?}, {height?, glassDepth, woodDepth}, {height?}] }, top to bottom. A band missing `height` splits the side's remaining clear height evenly. null (the default) means both sides are plain.

furnitureParams_coat-rack.description: Params for `coat-rack` (src/furniture/small-items.js, TYPES['coat-rack']): a wall hook rail with 0-3 simple draped coats. `height` is the FULL assembly: the rail is a fixed-height band at the top of it, and any draped coats hang from the rail down toward y=0 within that same declared height -- never below it. Each `default` equals the module's DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm.

height.description: cm, the full assembly (rail band plus any draped coats' drop).

coats.description: How many draped coats hang from the rail.

coatColors.description: Cycled across the coats, one per hook.

coatHeight.description: cm, the coat's own drop below the rail, clamped to stay within the declared `height` (never crosses y=0).

furnitureParams_digital-piano.description: Params for `digital-piano` (src/furniture/digital-piano.js): a slim white 88-key digital piano on its matching panel stand (two solid side panels and a back board), with 36 individual black keys, a lit display, speaker grilles and a small music rest. Each `default` equals digital-piano.js's PIANO_DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

height.description: cm, floor to the top of the music rest -- honoured exactly.

caseTopHeight.description: cm, floor to the top of the case (the control panel). The white keys sit 3 below it.

caseHeight.description: cm, the case itself, top to bottom; the stand runs from the floor to its underside.

keyDepth.description: cm, front-to-back length of a white key.

restWidth.description: cm, width of the music rest (a small centred panel).

restLean.description: Degrees the music rest leans back, away from the player.

sidePanelDepth.description: cm, front-to-back depth of the stand's solid side panels.

screenColor.description: The lit display on the control panel.

grilleColor.description: The speaker grilles at both ends of the control panel.

furnitureParams_dining-chair.description: Params for `dining-chair` (src/furniture/dining.js, TYPES['dining-chair']): a 90-degree WEDGE (quadrant) of a cylinder -- four of these, tucked in around a common centre, form the black cylinder a `dining-table` top sits on like a lid. `radius` is the arc's radius (also this wedge's `depth`); `backSweep` is the arc's angular span in degrees (`width` derives as 2*radius*sin(backSweep/2)). Each `default` equals dining.js's DEFAULTS for this key (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm, DERIVED from radius/backSweep: 2*radius*sin(backSweep/2). Carried as a schema default (rather than computed) because the validator does not run JS.

depth.description: cm, equals `radius` -- apex (front) to the back-arc's centre.

height.description: cm, floor to the HIGHEST point of the curved back shell (its centre -- the shell tapers lower toward the sides). Capped so 4 of these, tucked under a dining-table at its own DEFAULTS height (75cm, minus its 2.8cm top slab), clear the tabletop's underside by about 1cm.

radius.description: cm, the wedge's arc radius -- also its `depth`. Four chairs at this radius, tucked in, form a cylinder of this radius.

backSweep.description: degrees, the arc's angular span, centred on straight back. 84 (not a full quarter circle) leaves a 6-degree gap centred on each of the 4 seams between chairs tucked at 0/90/180/270 degrees -- room for the companion dining-table's own legs, which assume this value (see dining.js's leg-placement comment). A caller who changes this away from 84 without also adjusting the table's leg geometry can reopen the collision the gap exists to avoid.

seatHeight.description: cm, floor to the top of the seat. Clamped below `height`.

furnitureParams_dining-table.description: Params for `dining-table` (src/furniture/dining.js, TYPES['dining-table']): a round white top on FOUR splayed square legs (no pedestal), joined by a low crossbar frame -- modelled from a kitchen photo of a space-saving nesting set. `width` and `depth` both carry the diameter -- a round footprint only has one horizontal size, but the builder contract's bbox check needs both keys present and equal. Each `default` equals dining.js's DEFAULTS for this key (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm, the round top's diameter (kept equal to `depth`).

depth.description: cm, the round top's diameter (kept equal to `width`).

height.description: cm, floor to the top of the tabletop.

frameHeight.description: cm, floor to the crossbar frame's centre.

furnitureParams_fridge-freezer.description: Params for `fridge-freezer` (src/furniture/kitchen.js): a full-height two-door housing on the base runs' recessed plinth. Its default height is a typical wall units' top line, 210; for another line set `height` to it. Set `depth` to the neighbouring run's so its plinth face and plinth LED line up. Each `default` equals kitchen.js DEFAULTS.

width.description: cm, along the wall / the item's local x.

height.description: cm, floor to top -- the wall units' top line, to line up with them.

frontFinish.description: Palette finish of the fronts, carcass and plinth.

handleStyle.description: `bar`: D-bar handles. `knob`: small pulls. `rail`: handleless, one continuous J-rail under the worktop (wall units then have none). `none`: push-to-open.

freezerHeight.description: cm, the freezer door; the fridge door takes the rest.

plinthHeight.description: cm, the same kickboard as the base runs.

hinge.description: The doors hang from this edge; the handles go on the other.

plinthLed.description: An LED strip on its plinth, to carry a run's plinth strip past it. Static emissive in the builder's own colour: it follows no light. A strip that follows a Home Assistant light is a room light fixture on its own channel instead (docs/house-profile.md, "Kitchen LED strips"); turn this off then, or the line is drawn twice.

topLed.description: An LED strip on its top, to carry a wall run's top strip over it. Static emissive in the builder's own colour: it follows no light. A strip that follows a Home Assistant light is a room light fixture on its own channel instead (docs/house-profile.md, "Kitchen LED strips"); turn this off then, or the line is drawn twice.

furnitureParams_gaming-chair.description: Params for `gaming-chair` (src/furniture/gaming-chair.js): a racing-style gaming chair, size L. Each `default` equals gaming-chair.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs). seatHeight / reclineDeg / armHeight must lie in the ranges given here; the builder also clamps to them.

primaryColor.description: The colourway: seat cushion, seat bolsters, backrest front incl. the shoulder wings.

frameColor.description: Armrests, recline lever, gas lift, mechanism, 5-star base and casters.

labelColor.description: Wordmark strip on the neck pillow.

seatHeight.description: cm, floor to the top of the seat cushion.

reclineDeg.description: Degrees between seat and backrest; 90 is upright.

armHeight.description: cm, top of the arm pads above the seat top.

backrestHeight.description: cm, height of the backrest itself.

backrestWidth.description: cm, backrest width at the shoulder wings.

width.description: cm, overall envelope at the default pose (the armrest span). Descriptive: the builder does not read it.

height.description: cm, overall envelope at the default pose (floor to backrest top). Descriptive: the builder does not read it.

depth.description: cm, overall envelope at the default pose (backrest back to caster tip). Descriptive: the builder does not read it.

furnitureParams_hex-panel-cluster.description: Params for `hex-panel-cluster` (src/furniture/wall-panels.js): a honeycomb cluster of regular hexagon felt panels, one mesh per hex sharing a single geometry instance per cluster (29 meshes sharing one geometry at the living-room default). Each `default` equals wall-panels.js TYPES['hex-panel-cluster'].DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs). `width`, `height` and `depth` are DERIVED from `side`, `columns` and `thickness` (the cluster's own bbox) -- the validator cannot run JavaScript, so these three carry the pre-computed values for the DEFAULT cluster only; a house that changes `side` or `columns` gets the real derived bbox at render time, and the footprint checks that read `width`/`height` from a placed item's schema defaults will be approximate for a customised cluster.

columns.description: Hex count per column, left to right. The living-room default is a 29-hex cluster: 3,4,5,4,4,4,3,2 (flat-top hexes, stacked vertically within a column).

columnOffsets.description: Optional per-column shift, in half-hex units (positive = down), added on top of the automatic per-column centring. Same length as `columns`, or null (every column simply centred). The living-room default centres every column except column 5 (index 4), shifted down half a hex so it interlocks with columns 4 and 6 (both, like it, 4 hexes -- centring all three would leave them level with no honeycomb notch between them).

thickness.description: cm, panel depth off the wall.

color.description: Dark green felt, tuned for the LIVE APP across FOUR light states (review round 6, 2026-09-27). Round 5's #5a828c was tuned in only one light state (night, warm room light) and did not generalise: it rendered teal in daylight and blue at noon with the lights off, both in the demo house and the real living room the reference photos are of. This value was verified across night-lit, morning-lit, noon-lit and noon-lights-off and held dark green in every one (hue 124-157, brightness 0.25-0.34 of the wall, matching the reference photo's own ~0.23). Earlier values (#1e3228 round 2, #0a2515 round 3-4) were judged on the spec page, which reads noticeably brighter than the app for the same base colour: specs/spec-three.jsx installs a CubeCamera and sets scene.environment, giving every material image-based lighting from the room's own background -- the live app has no such environment map. The spec page renders this value as a lighter sage green (rgb ~80,113,95) due to that environment map -- accepted; aligning the spec page's own lighting with the app is a separate follow-up.

bevelWidth.description: cm, how far in from each hex's own outer edge the chamfer starts -- the front (plateau) face is inset by this much on every side. Modelled as a custom prism (NOT THREE.ExtrudeGeometry's own bevelEnabled, which grows the footprint outward): the hex's outer footprint and the column/row layout pitch, both keyed to `side` alone, are unaffected by this or `bevelDepth`.

bevelDepth.description: cm, how much thinner the rim is than the centre (must be < `thickness`) -- where two hexes meet, this is what forms the visible V-groove border line. About half of the default 1cm `thickness`.

width.description: cm. DERIVED from `side` + `columns` (the cluster's bbox) -- do not set independently of them. Value shown is the default cluster's own bbox width. Unaffected by bevelWidth/bevelDepth (the bevel insets the FRONT FACE only, never the outer footprint).

height.description: cm. DERIVED from `side` + `columns` (the cluster's bbox) -- do not set independently of them. Value shown is the default cluster's own bbox height.

furnitureParams_kitchen-base-run.description: Params for `kitchen-base-run` (src/furniture/kitchen.js): floor units under one continuous worktop, laid out left to right as you stand facing the run. Each `default` equals kitchen.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm, along the wall / the item's local x. Authoritative: modules that add up to less get a filler at the end away from the corner, and modules that add up to more are scaled to fit, with a warning either way.

height.description: cm, the run's whole ENVELOPE: floor to the top of the tallest part. With a sink that has a tap, that is the tap's top (worktopHeight + the tap, e.g. + 30); with no tap it is the worktop's top, and the worktop is drawn there.

worktopHeight.description: cm, floor to the top of the worktop, when a tap rises above it to `height`. Ignored (with a warning) when there is no tap to fill the space between them.

kind.description: `sink` is a sink centred on this one module (for one spanning modules use the run-level `sink`). `gap` is a bare space under the worktop: no carcass, front or plinth.

width.description: cm. Common sizes are 60 and a narrow 34.

hinge.description: cabinet / sink: `left` or `right` is one door hung from that edge, whatever its width (handle on the other edge); `top` is one lift-up flap (handle along its bottom); `bottom` is one drop-down front (handle along its top, like a dishwasher). With no hinge a cabinet over 60 cm has two doors.

hob.description: oven: a flush hob in the worktop above it.

bowl.description: sink: inset (metal rim flush with the worktop) or undermount.

plinthLed.description: An LED strip on the plinth under this module. Adjacent flagged modules share one strip; on the owner's flagged corner module it turns the corner to meet the other run's strip. Static emissive in the builder's own colour: it follows no light. A strip that follows a Home Assistant light is a room light fixture on its own channel instead (docs/house-profile.md, "Kitchen LED strips"); turn this off then, or the line is drawn twice.

drainer.description: sink: which side the drainer is, when the module is wide enough for one.

modules.description: Left to right as you stand facing the run (local +x).

corner.description: The end at which this run OWNS a corner: the leg whose worktop runs into the corner to the side wall, with a blind `corner` module there. Exactly one leg of an L owns it; the other is `none` and starts at the owner's front face.

cornerDepth.description: cm, the depth of the OTHER run at this run's corner (runs may differ). It is how much of the blind corner unit that run hides, and where this run's plinth return and LED turn. The corner module is widened to at least this, from its neighbour, so the other run cannot clash with it.

frontFinish.description: Palette finish of the fronts, carcass and plinth.

handleStyle.description: `bar`: D-bar handles. `knob`: small pulls. `rail`: handleless, one continuous J-rail under the worktop (wall units then have none). `none`: push-to-open.

plinthHeight.description: cm, the kickboard under the doors.

ledColor.description: Colour of the plinth LED strip under modules flagged `plinthLed`.

sink.description: A sink placed along the RUN rather than inside one module, so a 90 cm inset sink can span a cabinet and the dishwasher beside it. null = none (a `sink` module is the one-module shorthand). A tap (the default) needs `height` above `worktopHeight`.

at.description: cm from the run's LEFT end to the sink's centre. Moved inside the run, with a warning, if it does not fit.

width.description: cm, the whole sink including any drainer (default 90).

bowl.description: inset (default): a metal plate flush with the worktop. undermount: the bowl alone under the worktop's cut edge.

drainer.description: inset only: which side of the bowl the drainer is (default right; none under 70 cm).

furnitureParams_kitchen-wall-run.description: Params for `kitchen-wall-run` (src/furniture/kitchen.js): wall units of mixed heights with their tops aligned, plus an extractor hood. `elevation` (set by the placer) is the bottom of the tallest module. Each `default` equals kitchen.js DEFAULTS. Wall runs do not corner: each unit hangs whole on its own wall.

width.description: cm, along the wall / the item's local x. Authoritative, as for `kitchen-base-run`.

height.description: cm, the run's whole ENVELOPE: from the bottom of whatever hangs lowest (a module, or a hood's splashback) to the top line every module hangs from. The placer's `elevation` is that bottom; elevationForTop() in kitchen.js turns a shared top line into it.

kind.description: `gap` takes up width and draws nothing (bare wall).

width.description: cm.

at.description: cm from the run's LEFT end to this module's left edge. Without it a module follows the one before (the first starts at 0). Lets a hood sit over the oven on an otherwise bare wall.

height.description: cm; defaults to the run's height and may not exceed it. With a hood splashback, give every module its own height.

hinge.description: cabinet: `left` or `right` is one door hung from that edge, whatever its width; `top` is one lift-up flap; `bottom` one drop-down front. With no hinge a cabinet over 60 cm has two doors.

style.description: hood: a chimney hood (flue up to the run's top) or a canopy under a short cabinet.

visor.description: chimney hood visor. `glass` is a real transparent part and costs a draw of its own; `smoked` merges.

underLed.description: cabinet / corner / filler: an LED strip under it, lighting the worktop. Continues round the corner like `plinthLed`. Static emissive in the builder's own colour: it follows no light. A strip that follows a Home Assistant light is a room light fixture on its own channel instead (docs/house-profile.md, "Kitchen LED strips"); turn this off then, or the line is drawn twice.

topLed.description: cabinet / corner / filler: an LED strip on top of it. Static emissive in the builder's own colour: it follows no light. A strip that follows a Home Assistant light is a room light fixture on its own channel instead (docs/house-profile.md, "Kitchen LED strips"); turn this off then, or the line is drawn twice.

splashback.description: hood: height in cm of a metal panel hung on the wall under the hood, down toward the worktop. It is part of this run, so the run's height reaches down to its bottom.

run.description: The key of the base run under this wall run, as the page or placer names its pieces.

module.description: The index of the base module to centre over.

alignTo.description: Centre this module over a base run's module AS DRAWN (resolveAlignment() in kitchen.js sets `at` from it), so it cannot drift when the base run is fitted.

modules.description: Left to right as you stand facing the run (local +x).

fill.description: What the width the modules leave unused shows: `bare` wall (a hood alone on a wall) or `filler` panels.

frontFinish.description: Palette finish of the fronts, carcass and plinth.

handleStyle.description: `bar`: D-bar handles. `knob`: small pulls. `rail`: handleless, one continuous J-rail under the worktop (wall units then have none). `none`: push-to-open.

underLedColor.description: Colour of the under-cabinet strips. Each LED colour in a kitchen is a draw of its own.

topLedColor.description: Colour of the strips on top of the cabinets.

furnitureParams_mirror.description: Params for `mirror` (src/furniture/small-items.js, TYPES['mirror']): round, rect, pebble or triangle, with a frame. Each `default` equals the module's DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm.

height.description: cm.

furnitureParams_model.description: Params for `model` (src/furniture/model.js): a piece drawn from a .glb file that lives in the house profile, fitted into width x depth x height. Use it for a real product model the repo may not redistribute; decimate it first (scripts/model-lod). Each `default` equals the module's DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

src.description: Profile-relative path to a .glb, e.g. "assets/models/chair/lod.glb". No leading slash, no '..', no percent-encoded '..' (%2e%2e), no URL scheme; .glb only. A missing or unloadable file skips the item with a warning.

width.description: cm, along the wall / the item's local x.

height.description: cm.

fit.description: stretch: each axis scaled to its own dimension (the bbox is the envelope). contain: one uniform scale, the largest that fits.

yaw.description: Degrees, anticlockwise seen from above, applied before fitting: turns the file's front to face glTF +z (the item's front).

color.description: Override every primitive's colour (tints vertex colours). null keeps the file's colours.

maxTriangles.description: Refuse (skip, with a warning) a file with more triangles than this per LOD.

furnitureParams_monitor.description: Params for `monitor` (src/furniture/small-items.js, TYPES['monitor']): flat or curved super-ultrawide, with an optional riser. `height` and `depth` are the FULL assembly: with `riser` enabled, set `height` to include the riser and stand below the panel, and set `depth` to at least `riserDepth` (the riser is typically the deepest part). Each `default` equals the module's DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm.

height.description: cm, the full assembly including its own stand (and riser, if any).

depth.description: cm, the full assembly -- must be at least `riserDepth` when `riser` is set, or the riser is clamped to fit and reads shallower than requested.

riserDepth.description: cm, clamped to at most the declared `depth`.

curveRadius.description: cm. 0 keeps the shallow segmented bow; above 0 (with `curved`) builds a true arc of this radius -- 1000R is 100 -- with a rear housing, a neck and a flat foot. The params below marked 'arc only' apply to that build.

panelHeight.description: cm, arc only: the panel alone; the rest of `height` is the stand (and riser).

panelDepth.description: cm, arc only: the set's depth WITHOUT its stand (the curve's sag, the panel and the rear housing).

bezel.description: cm, arc only: the bezel round the active area.

backColor.description: Arc only: the back shell and rear housing.

standColor.description: Arc only: the neck and foot.

footWidth.description: cm, arc only: the pentagon foot's widest point.

footDepth.description: cm, arc only: the foot, from its rear point (z = 0) to its front edge.

coreLight.description: Arc only: a glowing ring on the back round the neck's joint.

furnitureParams_ottoman.description: Params for `ottoman` (src/furniture/digital-piano.js, TYPES['ottoman']): a simple velvet ottoman with a channel-tufted lid, on four short legs. Each `default` equals the module's OTTOMAN_DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

channelCount.description: Channel-tufted ridges across the lid, front-to-back.

channelDepth.description: cm, how far each ridge stands proud of the flat lid.

furnitureParams_pc-tower.description: Params for `pc-tower` (src/furniture/small-items.js, TYPES['pc-tower']): a box-ish tower with an optional glass side panel. Each `default` equals the module's DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm.

height.description: cm.

interiorColor.description: The motherboard, CPU cooler and graphics card seen through the glass (the PSU shroud is in `color`).

furnitureParams_photo-frame.description: Params for `photo-frame` (src/furniture/small-items.js, TYPES['photo-frame']): 1-N panels of picture-frame artwork. `image` is a URL relative to the HOUSE dir, loaded (by the live scene, never by this schema or the builder contract test) as a texture on a kept panel; a plain colour panel otherwise. Each `default` equals the module's DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm, the whole run of panels.

height.description: cm.

panels.description: How many equal panels split `width`, e.g. 5 for a multi-panel artwork.

color.description: The plain-colour fallback panel, used when `image` is unset or fails to load.

image.description: A URL relative to the HOUSE dir. No leading slash, no `..`, no absolute URL -- the same rule as textures and overlays.

furnitureParams_piano-bench.description: Params for `piano-bench` (src/furniture/digital-piano.js, TYPES['piano-bench']): a classic adjustable piano bench -- a button-tufted faux-leather seat with rolled edges, an apron with an adjustment knob at each end, four square tapered legs. Each `default` equals the module's BENCH_DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

height.description: cm, floor to the top of the seat.

apronHeight.description: cm, the apron under the seat (the height mechanism).

baseColor.description: The frame: apron, knobs and legs.

furnitureParams_plant.description: Params for `plant` (src/furniture/plant.js): a procedural potted or wall-mounted plant. Each `default` equals plant.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs). width/depth/height are the authoritative bounding envelope the builder fits its procedural geometry onto exactly; the other numbers proportion the interior detail for the `kind` in use.

kind.description: corn-plant: a potted Dracaena, canes crowned by tufts of long leaves. wall-planter: a geometric wall planter (ceramic lower half, brass wire diamond). peace-lily: grown in water in a glass bubble vase. snake-plant: stiff sword leaves. pothos: heart leaves, upright or trailing (see habit/trail). ficus: a small thick-trunk tree. jade: a succulent with fleshy pads.

width.description: cm, along the wall / the item's local x -- the footprint envelope.

height.description: cm, floor (or `elevation`) to top. For a trailing pothos this INCLUDES `trail`: the vine tips are at y = 0.

potStyle.description: Free-standing kinds: the pot's shape. glass-bubble is clear glass (kept as its own draw). The peace-lily kind always uses glass-bubble.

potHeight.description: Free-standing kinds: pot height, cm (proportioning; width/depth/height are the final envelope).

potTopDiameter.description: Free-standing kinds: pot opening diameter, cm (proportioning).

potColor.description: Pot colour; for wall-planter, the ceramic.

plantHeight.description: Foliage height above the pot rim, cm (proportioning). corn-plant: the canes are fixed fractions of it (about 0.72 / 0.30 / 0.12 to their tops).

stemCount.description: corn-plant: canes. pothos: stems or vines. ficus: branches. jade: stems.

spread.description: Widest foliage spread, cm (proportioning). corn-plant: the top crown.

leafLength.description: Leaf length, cm. corn-plant: independent of spread -- a narrower spread bends the leaves steeper rather than shortening them.

leafCount.description: Leaves (peace-lily, snake-plant, pothos, ficus) or pads (jade). corn-plant and wall-planter set their own counts per cane / per `contents`.

accentColor.description: Variegation (peace-lily) and leaf margins (snake-plant; wall-planter contents snake-plant).

habit.description: pothos only: upright arching stems, or vines that hang over the rim.

trail.description: pothos trailing only: cm the vines hang BELOW the pot base. The pot base stands at exactly y = trail, so place the item with elevation = surface height - trail. At 0 nothing hangs below the pot. Capped at 0.95 x height (a larger trail puts the pot base at 0.95 x height).

contents.description: wall-planter only: a spiky tuft, a short succulent, or a few sword leaves with pale margins.

seed.description: Deterministic layout seed -- the same seed always lays out the same plant.

furnitureParams_radiator.description: Params for `radiator` (src/furniture/radiator.js): a white compact panel radiator with vertical ribs, a smart thermostatic valve on the END of the radiator at a chosen corner and a lockshield on the other end, pipes dropping from both, and an optional cover (a clip-on shelf with a raised front lip, or a framed slatted box). width/height/depth ALWAYS describe the WHOLE OUTER ENVELOPE -- body, end valves and cover; the pipes too, except that they continue `pipeDrop` cm below the bottom to reach the floor -- because scripts/validate-house.py's footprint/overlap/ceiling checks and src/furniture/place.js read these three params with no idea a body/valve/cover split exists. The end valves need room beside the body (12.1 cm on the smart-valve end, 5.9 cm on the other), so the default 98-wide envelope holds an 80-wide body. The optional bodyWidth/bodyHeight/bodyDepth describe the RADIATOR BODY itself, defaulting to a snug fit (the largest body the envelope leaves room for) and clamped strictly inside any cover. There is no `elevation` param here: a wall-hung radiator is placed by the furniture ITEM's own top-level `elevation` field ($defs/furnitureItem.elevation) -- an earlier `params.elevation` was dead and was removed, per item 2bc314c9. `bodyElevation` is different: it lifts the body INSIDE the envelope, for a floor-standing box cover. Each `default` equals radiator.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm, the OUTER ENVELOPE's width along the wall / the item's local x: the body, the room for both end valves, any shelf overrun, or the box cover.

height.description: cm, the OUTER ENVELOPE's height (always -- includes any cover and any bodyElevation), from the item's own local floor (y=0) to its top. Use the furniture item's own top-level `elevation` field to raise it off the room floor -- there is no params.elevation here.

depth.description: cm, the OUTER ENVELOPE's wall-to-front distance (always -- includes any cover). A shelf's front edge sits at this depth, overhanging the radiator's face.

bodyWidth.description: cm, the RADIATOR BODY's own width. Optional: defaults to a snug fit -- the envelope width minus the room both end valves (18 cm) or a longer shelf overrun need, and minus the box's side panels for a 'box' cover. A larger value is clamped down to that.

bodyHeight.description: cm, the RADIATOR BODY's own height. Optional: defaults to a snug fit -- the envelope height minus bodyElevation and minus what sits on top (3.6 cm for a shelf, 3 cm for a box's top board and clearance). A larger value is clamped down to that.

bodyDepth.description: cm, the RADIATOR BODY's own wall-to-front distance. Optional: defaults to a snug fit == `depth` with no cover, 1 cm less for a shelf (so the shelf overhangs the face), and 6.8 cm less for a box (so a real air gap stays in front of the body, behind the cover's backing).

thickness.description: cm, the radiator body's own slab depth (not including the wall gap). wallGap is derived as bodyDepth - thickness, never authored; thickness is itself clamped down to bodyDepth if given bigger.

valveCorner.description: Which corner carries the smart valve. The valve sits on that corner's END of the radiator, pointing outward along the wall; the lockshield sits at the BOTTOM of the other end, where the return pipe comes up from the floor.

cover.description: `shelf` = a clip-on wooden shelf resting on the radiator, with a raised lip along its front edge, overhanging the face; the sides stay open. `box` = a framed slatted cover standing on the floor: a top board overhanging the carcass, side panels, stiles that run to the floor as legs, a vent slot, vertical slats with a dark backing behind them, and an open kick-out under the bottom rail. The item's overall footprint is ALWAYS width/height/depth (the envelope), cover or not.

coverColor.description: The shelf's wood colour. A 'box' cover is white unless this is set away from its default.

bodyElevation.description: cm, the body's bottom INSIDE the envelope. Not a placement elevation (that is the item's own top-level `elevation`): it is for a floor-standing box cover, whose envelope starts at the floor while the radiator inside hangs higher. The pipes always run down to the envelope's bottom.

shelfExtendLeft.description: cm, how far a 'shelf' cover runs past the body's left end (seen from the front). The envelope must leave room for it; ignored for other covers.

shelfExtendRight.description: cm, how far a 'shelf' cover runs past the body's right end. Ignored for other covers.

boxKick.description: cm, the height of the open kick-out under a 'box' cover's bottom rail. Optional: min(12, 0.14 x height) when absent. 0 runs the bottom rail and the slat panel down to the floor with no kick-out (a box that stands on the floor). Clamped so the slat panel keeps some height. Ignored for other covers.

pipeDrop.description: cm the pipes continue BELOW the item's own bottom (y=0), so they reach the room floor. It must equal the item's top-level `elevation` (17 for a radiator hung 17 cm up; 0 for a floor-standing box cover), so LEAVE IT OUT: the furniture placer (src/furniture.js itemParams) sets it from the item's elevation whenever it is absent. An authored value wins. The pipes are the ONE part allowed outside width/height/depth, and only downward by exactly this much: they hug the wall beside the radiator's ends, inside the envelope's width and depth, so the footprint and ceiling checks are unaffected.

furnitureParams_robot-vacuum.description: Params for `robot-vacuum` (src/furniture/robot-vacuum.js): a round robot vacuum on a self-emptying dock -- a rounded tower at the back (white lower part, champagne metal band, white lid) on a base plate with a front ramp, the robot at the front with its rear tucked under the tower. `dock: false` draws the robot alone, filling the envelope; set width = depth = robotDiameter and height = robotHeight then. With the dock, the plate is exactly width x depth and the lid top is exactly height; every other part is clamped inside that envelope. Each `default` equals robot-vacuum.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm, the base plate's width (with the dock) or the robot's width (without).

depth.description: cm, back of the tower to the front of the robot.

height.description: cm, floor to the top of the tower lid (with the dock) or of the robot's lidar puck (without).

dock.description: false = the robot alone; the envelope is then the robot.

robotDiameter.description: cm, clamped to the smaller of width and depth.

robotHeight.description: cm, floor (or plate) to the top of the lidar puck; clamped to fit.

towerWidth.description: cm, the dock tower's width, clamped to width.

towerDepth.description: cm, the dock tower's depth from the back, clamped to depth.

bodyColor.description: Robot body, dock tower, lid and base plate.

bandColor.description: The band round the tower: a light champagne in a gloss finish (not metal, which renders it dark bronze).

puckColor.description: The lidar puck on the robot's top.

ledColor.description: The status LED (emissive, drawn on its own).

furnitureParams_shelf.description: Params for `shelf` (src/furniture/small-items.js, TYPES['shelf']): a floating shelf, with an optional LED edge, an optional stacked `levels` set, and an optional `backPanel` L-section (a floating shelf with a back panel against the wall). `height` is ALWAYS the full assembly: one slab's thickness with no `levels`, the WHOLE stack (every slab plus every gap) with `levels`, or the overall back-panel-to-shelf-top height with `backPanel`. Each slab's own thickness is the separate `shelfThickness` param. Each `default` equals the module's DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm.

height.description: cm, the FULL assembly -- see the block description for what that means per option.

shelfThickness.description: cm, ONE slab's own thickness -- independent of `height`, which is always the overall envelope.

levels.description: Explicit vertical gaps (cm) between stacked shelves, e.g. [30, 30] for a 3-shelf set. Empty = a single shelf. Set `height` to the sum of every `shelfThickness` slab plus every gap.

backPanel.description: An L-section: a vertical back panel against the wall plus the horizontal shelf slab. Applies to the bottom unit of a `levels` stack.

shelfColor.description: The horizontal slab's own colour when `backPanel` is set (independent of `color`, which is the plain single-shelf colour).

furnitureParams_shower-screen.description: Params for `shower-screen` (src/furniture/bathroom.js, TYPES['shower-screen']): framed glazing in one plane: a bath screen (`frame: rail` -- hinge jamb + top rail) or framed fixed panes and hinged doors with mullions (`frame: full`). Always drawn closed. Each `default` equals bathroom.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs). Generic, illustrative defaults; a real room's values live in its furniture[].params.

width.description: cm, along the wall / the item's local x.

height.description: cm, bottom to top.

panels.description: left to right as you face the screen; widths are scaled to fill `width`.

hinge.description: which end the jamb (rail) or each door's hinge (full) is at.

furnitureParams_shower-set.description: Params for `shower-set` (src/furniture/bathroom.js, TYPES['shower-set']): a thermostatic bar valve, riser rail, handset and hose, with an optional wall bath spout. Authored by FLOOR heights; `width`/`depth`/`height` are OUTPUTS -- set them, and the item's `elevation`, from showerSetEnvelope() in bathroom.js. Each `default` equals bathroom.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs). Generic, illustrative defaults; a real room's values live in its furniture[].params.

width.description: cm, along the wall / the item's local x.

height.description: cm, bottom to top.

valveHeight.description: cm, floor to the bar valve centreline.

riserOffset.description: cm along the wall from the valve centre to the riser; + is right as you face the wall.

riserFrom.description: cm, floor to the lower riser bracket.

riserTo.description: cm, floor to the upper riser bracket.

handsetHeight.description: cm, floor to the handset slider; null = 22 below riserTo.

spoutHeight.description: cm, floor to a wall bath spout under the valve; null = none.

spoutReach.description: cm the spout reaches out from the wall.

furnitureParams_shower-tray.description: Params for `shower-tray` (src/furniture/bathroom.js, TYPES['shower-tray']): a low rounded shower tray with a waste. Each `default` equals bathroom.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs). Generic, illustrative defaults; a real room's values live in its furniture[].params.

width.description: cm, along the wall / the item's local x.

height.description: cm, bottom to top.

furnitureParams_slat-panel.description: Params for `slat-panel` (src/furniture/wall-panels.js): vertical slat panelling over a felt backing, ported from the acoustic-panel look in src/home3d-scene.js. Each `default` equals wall-panels.js TYPES['slat-panel'].DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm, along the wall.

height.description: cm, floor (or `elevation`) to top.
