depth.description: cm. DERIVED: `backingDepth` + `slatDepth` (the felt backing plus how far the slats protrude off it) -- do not set independently of them.

slatWidth.description: cm, each slat's face width. Slats are fit to the whole `width`, redistributing any remainder into the gap so the run starts and ends on a slat. Default matches the real Acupanel Contemporary Oak product spec (src/home3d-scene.js's hard-coded bedroom panel).

pitch.description: cm, nominal centre-to-centre spacing (slat width + gap). The actual pitch is adjusted slightly so a whole number of slats fits `width`.

slatDepth.description: cm, how far each slat protrudes off the felt backing.

backingDepth.description: cm, the felt backing's own thickness, behind the slats.

finish.description: Applies to the slat mesh only -- the felt backing is always `matte`, hard-coded in the builder. Default `satin` (roughness 0.6) matches the bedroom's hard-coded panel (roughness 0.55) more closely than `matte` (0.8) would.

grainMap.description: Adds a subtle procedural oak-grain roughness map to the slats, matching the bedroom's hard-coded panel (src/home3d-scene.js). Off by default; the spec page's oak preset turns it on. A narrow, deliberate exception to the finish palette (src/furniture/finishes.js) -- there is no grained finish key.

furnitureParams_sofa.description: Params for `sofa` (src/furniture/sofa.js): a corner (L-shaped) sofa -- fabric seat and back cushions on a plinth base, a low padded arm at the non-chaise end, and a chaise running forward to the full `depth` (no arm or back on its outer end). `chaise: 'none'` is a straight sofa with an arm at both ends whose depth is the whole `depth` (set depth = seatDepth for one). Every part is clamped so any params build to exactly width x depth x height. Each `default` equals sofa.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm, overall width including the arm(s) and the chaise.

depth.description: cm, back to the front of the chaise (or of the seat, for a straight sofa).

height.description: cm, floor to the top of the back cushions.

chaise.description: Which end the chaise is at, seen from the FRONT (+x is the viewer's right). 'none' is a straight sofa.

seatDepth.description: cm, depth of the main (non-chaise) leg.

chaiseWidth.description: cm, width of the chaise leg.

seatHeight.description: cm, floor to the top of the seat cushions.

baseHeight.description: cm, floor to the top of the plinth base.

armHeight.description: cm, floor to the top of the arm pad.

cushions.description: Seat cushions across the main leg.

baseFinish.description: Finish of the plinth base and arm body (satin reads as faux leather).

furnitureParams_speaker.description: Params for `speaker` (src/furniture/small-items.js, TYPES['speaker']): four kinds selected by `kind`. `width` is always the OVERALL (widest) footprint width -- for `wall-trapezoid` that is the back edge (`frontWidth` is the narrower front). `ceiling` is geometry only; see the builder's own comment for how a placer should orient it (elevation + rotation, no new placement mechanism). Each `default` equals the module's DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm, the overall (widest) footprint width.

height.description: cm.

frontWidth.description: wall-trapezoid only: the narrower front edge.

boxShape.description: wall-trapezoid only: swap the trapezoid plan for a plain box.

grille.description: wall-trapezoid, floor-standing and centre: a smoked see-through grille over the drivers, inside the front rim. false keeps the rim and shows the drivers bare.

port.description: wall-trapezoid and floor-standing: a round bass port on the baffle below the drivers.

plinthWidth.description: floor-standing only: the outrigger plinth footprint, capped to `width`/`depth`.

midDrivers.description: floor-standing only: bass/mid discs below the top tweeter.

firing.description: ceiling only: which face carries the driver.

furnitureParams_standing-desk.description: Params for `standing-desk` (src/furniture/standing-desk.js): a sit-stand desk, rectangular top on two T-foot telescoping legs. width/depth/height are the OVERALL ENVELOPE at the default pose (height = topHeight + topThickness); topHeight is the separate sit-stand-adjustable input, clamped to [minHeight, maxHeight]. Each `default` equals standing-desk.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm, along the wall / the item's local x.

height.description: cm, floor (or `elevation`) to the top surface, at the default pose: topHeight + topThickness.

topHeight.description: cm, floor to the underside of the desk top -- the sit-stand-adjustable input, clamped to [minHeight, maxHeight].

topThickness.description: cm, thickness of the desk top slab.

controlSide.description: Which side of the front edge the control panel sits on, as seen by a person standing at the front of the desk facing it. Its outer edge sits 4cm in from the desk's side edge on that side.

ledStrip.description: Draw an LED strip tucked under the desktop's edge (one continuous run along `ledSides`). Emissive only and static: a preview of the look. A desk strip that follows a Home Assistant light is a room light fixture on its own channel instead (docs/house-profile.md).

ledSides.description: Which edges the strip runs along, as seen from the front of the desk. Default: down the left, across the front, up the right.

furnitureParams_subwoofer.description: Params for `subwoofer` (src/furniture/small-items.js, TYPES['subwoofer']): a cube on four short feet with one front-firing woofer and a bass port behind a see-through grille in a front rim. Each `default` equals the module's DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm.

height.description: cm.

grille.description: A smoked see-through grille over the woofer and port, inside the front rim.

port.description: A round bass port below the woofer.

furnitureParams_toilet.description: Params for `toilet` (src/furniture/bathroom.js, TYPES['toilet']): a back-to-wall WC: lofted pan, square soft-close seat and lid, and an optional flush plate on the wall behind it. `height` is the envelope: the flush plate's top (with no plate, the lid's top = seatHeight + 4.2). Each `default` equals bathroom.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs). Generic, illustrative defaults; a real room's values live in its furniture[].params.

width.description: cm, along the wall / the item's local x.

height.description: cm, bottom to top.

seatHeight.description: cm, floor to the top of the pan (the seat sits on it).

flushPlate.description: draw the flush plate on the wall behind the pan, its top at `height`.

furnitureParams_towel-rail.description: Params for `towel-rail` (src/furniture/bathroom.js, TYPES['towel-rail']): a chrome ladder towel rail standing on the floor against a wall. Each `default` equals bathroom.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs). Generic, illustrative defaults; a real room's values live in its furniture[].params.

width.description: cm, along the wall / the item's local x.

height.description: cm, bottom to top.

furnitureParams_tube-floor-lamp.description: Params for `tube-floor-lamp` (src/furniture/small-items.js, TYPES['tube-floor-lamp']): a thin emissive light tube rising from a small cylinder base. `width`/`depth` are the OVERALL footprint (the base, the widest part), not the thin tube. Each `default` equals the module's DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm, the base's diameter (the overall footprint).

height.description: cm, base plus tube.

oneSidedGlow.description: An open half-tube (glows from one side only) instead of a full cylinder.

furnitureParams_tv.description: Params for `tv` (src/furniture/small-items.js, TYPES['tv']): a wall TV. `bezelStyle: 'thin'` is a plain flat panel (optionally on a pedestal `stand` instead of wall-mounted); `'picture-frame'` is a wooden picture-frame bezel (Frame-TV look), wall-hung. "Art mode" imagery is not built yet. Generic defaults only -- real dimensions come from a research note, never a model name, which never appears in this repo. Each `default` equals the module's DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs).

width.description: cm.

height.description: cm, the FULL assembly: with `stand` enabled this includes the pedestal below the panel.

depth.description: cm, the full assembly -- with `stand` enabled, set at least `standDepth` (the pedestal foot is typically the deepest part).

stand.description: thin style only: a central pedestal stand instead of wall-mounting.

standDepth.description: cm, clamped to at most the declared `depth`.

furnitureParams_vanity-counter.description: Params for `vanity-counter` (src/furniture/bathroom.js, TYPES['vanity-counter']): a boxed vanity counter / duct with a countertop, an optional semi-recessed basin let into a notch in the countertop and a mono mixer. `depth` is the envelope (counterDepth + how far the basin stands proud); `height` is the tap's top (vanityEnvelope() in bathroom.js). Each `default` equals bathroom.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs). Generic, illustrative defaults; a real room's values live in its furniture[].params.

width.description: cm, along the wall / the item's local x.

height.description: cm, bottom to top.

counterDepth.description: cm, wall to the counter face.

counterHeight.description: cm, floor to the countertop top.

basinDepth.description: cm, clamped so its back clears the wall by 1 cm.

basinHeight.description: cm, rim to the bowl underside.

basinAt.description: cm from the counter's LEFT end (as you face it) to the basin centre; null = centred.

basinLip.description: cm the rim stands above the countertop.

tap.description: a mono mixer on the basin deck, rising to `height`.

tileWidth.description: cm, grout-line pitch on the counter face; 0 = none.

furnitureParams_wall-clock.description: Params for `wall-clock` (src/furniture/wall-clock.js): a working wall clock in three styles -- `framed` (a round face + rim + hands), `diy-numerals` (numerals/dots stuck straight on the wall around a plain hands unit, matching a photo of a real DIY wall clock), or `diy-words` (a frameless stick-on clock -- big numerals at 12/9/6, dots at 7/8/10/11, the words "One" to "Five" to the right of the 1-5 ring positions, a centre disc, tapered hands and a red second hand -- matching the owner's actual kitchen clock, item 059873ed). `time` only sets the hands' pose at BUILD time; a live scene re-poses them continuously via wall-clock.js's exported setClockTime(group, date) helper. Each `default` equals wall-clock.js's DEFAULTS for this key (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs) -- `diy-words`'s OWN defaults (wider width/height, to include the words) live in the module's separately-exported DIY_WORDS_DEFAULTS, the same two-defaults-objects pattern wall-sconce.js uses for its own second kind. `x-kindDefaults` carries diy-words' width/height for scripts/validate-house.py, and a diy-words item starts from them on the house path (wall-clock.js defaultsFor; scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs keeps them equal).

width.description: cm, kept equal to `diameter` for `framed`/`diy-numerals`. For `diy-words` this is the WHOLE envelope including the words that extend right of the ring (49.8cm at the DIY_WORDS_DEFAULTS diameter of 30cm), not the ring diameter alone.

depth.description: cm, how far the clock protrudes from the wall.

height.description: cm, kept equal to `diameter` for `framed`/`diy-numerals`. For `diy-words` this includes headroom above/below the ring for the 12/6 numerals (39cm at the DIY_WORDS_DEFAULTS diameter of 30cm).

kind.description: `framed`: a conventional round face, rim and hands. `diy-numerals`: numerals/dots stuck directly on the wall around a plain hands unit, no face disc. `diy-words`: a frameless stick-on clock with numerals, dots AND words, matching the owner's actual kitchen clock -- see the block description.

diameter.description: cm, the RING's diameter -- kept equal to `width`/`height` for `framed`/`diy-numerals` only; `diy-words`'s width/height are the wider full envelope (see those fields).

secondHandColor.description: The second hand's own colour -- defaults to `handColor` when not set, EXCEPT `diy-words`, whose DIY_WORDS_DEFAULTS sets this red while the other hands stay black (the owner's photo).

time.description: "HH:MM", 24-hour. Sets the hour/minute hands' pose at build time ONLY (seconds default to 0) -- see the block description for how a live scene keeps the clock running.

furnitureParams_wall-sconce.description: Params for `wall-sconce` (src/furniture/wall-sconce.js): ONE registered type covering two visual kinds selected by `kind`. `default`s below are the 'swing-arm-globe' kind's DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs); `x-kindDefaults` gives the 'up-down' kind's own envelope, which an item of that kind starts from (wall-sconce.js defaultsFor; the same test keeps the two equal). The 'up-down' kind's own fields (bodyWidth, bodyHeight, bodyDepth, plateThickness, lensDiameter, lensProtrusion) are listed too, with no `default` of their own, so an 'up-down' item can set them without additionalProperties rejecting it; wall-sconce.js's own UP_DOWN_DEFAULTS is the source of truth for their values when `kind` is 'up-down'.

armLength.description: cm, swing-arm-globe only: horizontal projection of the arm off the wall.

dropLength.description: cm, swing-arm-globe only: vertical drop from the arm to the globe cap.

glassColor.description: swing-arm-globe only: smoked/amber glass shade colour.

plateThickness.description: cm, up-down only: backplate thickness. See UP_DOWN_DEFAULTS in wall-sconce.js.

bodyWidth.description: cm, up-down only: the raised body's width. See UP_DOWN_DEFAULTS in wall-sconce.js.

bodyHeight.description: cm, up-down only: the raised body's height. See UP_DOWN_DEFAULTS in wall-sconce.js.

bodyDepth.description: cm, up-down only: how far the body stands off the backplate. See UP_DOWN_DEFAULTS in wall-sconce.js.

lensDiameter.description: cm, up-down only: the top/bottom lens diameter. See UP_DOWN_DEFAULTS in wall-sconce.js.

lensProtrusion.description: cm, up-down only: how far each lens stands proud of the body. See UP_DOWN_DEFAULTS in wall-sconce.js.

on.description: Emissive glow only (bulb, or the up-down kind's two lenses + faint beam-cone hints) -- no THREE light is added by the builder.

width.description: cm, overall bbox width.

depth.description: cm, overall bbox depth (projection off the wall).

height.description: cm, overall bbox height.

furnitureParams_wall-sign.description: Params for `wall-sign` (src/furniture/wall-sign.js): a framed sign with a two-line CanvasTexture text panel, two depth levels (outer frame + inner panel/body). `default`s equal wall-sign.js DEFAULTS (enforced by scripts/test-furniture-defaults.mjs). line1/line2 default to a stock retail sign phrase, not any real house's wording; house-specific wording, if different, lives only in a private overlay outside this repo.

width.description: cm, overall frame width (landscape).

height.description: cm, overall frame height.

depth.description: cm, OUTER FRAME depth (front to back), back at z=0 -- the sign's frontmost surface.

panelDepth.description: cm, inner panel/body depth. Its own front (text) face sits at z=panelDepth, so the frame projects forward past it by (depth - panelDepth).

frameThickness.description: cm, width of the frame member around the panel.

lightFixture.title: A light fixture group within a room
lightFixture.description:
One controllable group of lights in a room — the thing that maps 1:1 to a Home Assistant light entity. A room typically has a 'main' group and may have others.

The `channel` field is the join to rooms.json: geometry says WHERE the bedroom's ambient lights are, rooms.json says WHICH entity switches them. The pair (room id, channel) is the composite key.

Fixture POSITIONS are explicit here. The reference implementation hardcoded them per-room-id inside the renderer (a chain of `if (id === "living_room")` blocks placing downlights at literal coordinates), which is exactly what makes it another person's-house-only. Listing positions as data is the single biggest thing that makes the engine reusable.

channel.description: Which lighting channel this group is. 'main' is the room's primary ceiling light. 'ambient' is indirect/accent lighting (strips, cove, sconces). Anything else is a named special — the reference house has a 'galaxy' star projector in the bedroom — and is treated as its own independently-switchable group. Must be unique within a room.

label.description: Display name for this group, e.g. "Bedroom Ambience".

fixtureType.description: The visible fixture the engine draws at each position. 'downlight' = flush ceiling disc; 'spot' = surface-mounted spot; 'pendant' = hanging bulb; 'strip' = a linear LED run (uses `size`); 'bulb' = a bare E27-style bulb; 'projector' = a special effect emitter (the galaxy light); 'none' = light with no visible fixture geometry.

colorTemperatureK.description: Nominal colour temperature in kelvin, used to tint the emitted light when HA does not report one.

positions.description: Where the individual fixtures in this group sit. Each entry is an explicit position, so a five-downlight kitchen lists five entries. If omitted, the engine falls back to auto-placing `count` fixtures on a grid over the room polygon — convenient when starting out, but the result is generic; list positions once you care how it looks.

heightCm.description: Height above this room's floor, in centimetres. Omit for a ceiling fixture (the engine places it just below the ceiling). Needed for a wall-mounted strip or an under-desk light.

label.description: What this individual fixture is, in the owner's own words — "under the left desk", "curtain cornice", "behind TV". Descriptive only; it is what makes a positions list readable a year later.

size.description: For fixtureType 'strip': the emitter's [length, height, depth] in centimetres, so a 2 m cornice run reads as a line rather than a point.

drawn.description: For fixtureType 'strip': false draws no emitter mesh, only the light. Use it when a furniture item draws the strip itself and follows the same channel (a bedside table channel with `light`, cabinet.js), so the line is not drawn twice.

reachCm.description: For fixtureType 'strip': how far the light reaches, in centimetres (its cut-off distance; default 250). A small light tucked into furniture wants a short reach.

aim.description: For fixtureType 'strip': a plan direction [dx, dy] (x east, y south) the light faces. The light becomes a shadowless spot that lights only within `spreadDeg` of it -- a bedside table level's light faces out of the table, so it washes the fronts beside it and the floor in front but never reaches straight up or down to the other level's channel.

spreadDeg.description: With `aim`: the spot's half-angle in degrees (default 90: the whole half-space the light faces).

count.description: How many fixtures to auto-place when `positions` is absent. Ignored when `positions` is given.

roomLights.description: The lighting groups for one room.

room.description: Which room these fixtures are in. Must be an id present in `rooms`.

cameraPreset.description: A named camera pose, in orbit coordinates around the model's centre.

azimuth.description: Orbit angle in radians around the vertical axis. 0 puts the camera on the +X (east) side looking west; π/2 puts it on the +Z (south) side looking north.

polar.description: Angle from straight-up, in radians. Near 0 is top-down (use a small non-zero value — an exactly-vertical lookAt is degenerate); π/2 is eye level.

distance.description: Camera distance from the target, in METRES (world units, not plan centimetres) — this is a camera property, not a plan measurement.

target.description: Optional plan-space point to orbit around. Defaults to the centre of the footprint computed from the walls, which is the right answer for almost every house.

schemaVersion.description: Version of THIS schema that the profile was written against, as MAJOR.MINOR. The engine refuses a profile whose MAJOR it does not know, and may run a migration for an older MINOR. Bump MINOR for additive changes, MAJOR for anything that changes the meaning of an existing field.

id.description: Profile id. Should match the directory name under houses/, because that is what HOME3D_HOUSE / ?house= select.

name.description: Human-readable name of the house, shown in the title overlay.

units.description: The unit every plan-space number in this file is expressed in. Only 'cm' is supported, deliberately: Sweet Home 3D exports centimetres, the reference data is centimetres, and allowing a second unit would double the number of places a conversion can be forgotten. Metres appear in exactly two places — camera `distance`, and the world-space output of `coordinateTransform` — and both say so explicitly.

defaults.description: House-wide defaults. Every field here is overridable on the individual room/wall/door; these exist so a profile does not have to repeat the same number a hundred times.

doorOpeningHeight.description: Height of the hole cut in the wall, cm. Slightly more than doorHeight; the wall above remains as a lintel.

doorFrameReveal.description: Frame reveal each side of the opening, cm.

doorRestOpenFraction.description: House-wide at-rest openness, as a fraction of each door's solved maximum. NOTE this applies only to doors that have a contact sensor bound in rooms.json: the renderer rests a door with NO sensor CLOSED regardless, because nothing reports its state. A per-door `restOpenFraction` overrides both.

ceilingHeight.description: Floor-to-ceiling height, cm. Defaults to wallHeight.

wallColor.description: Interior wall paint colour. If you know your actual paint, put its hex here; if you know only the product name, record that in `wallPaintName` and approximate the hex.

wallPaintName.description: The real product name of the wall paint, e.g. "<Brand> Vinyl Matt, Soft White". Documentation only — the engine renders `wallColor`. Retail paints rarely publish authoritative hex values, so keeping the name alongside the approximation records what the approximation is *of*.

doorSlabColor.description: Default colour for internal door leaves.

exteriorColor.description: Outward-facing colour of the exterior shell.

viewCentre.description:
OPTIONAL point the default cameras look at, and the centre of the ground plane and cloud field. Defaults to the middle of the wall footprint, which is right for most plans.

State it only when the geometric middle is not the point you want framed — a long thin projection (a hallway arm, an outhouse, an integral garage) drags the footprint's midpoint away from the part of the house someone actually looks at.

decor.description:
OPTIONAL bespoke decoration this house asks the engine to build, by name.

Decor is FURNITURE, not building fabric: it is geometry keyed to specific wall ids of a specific house, so it can be neither derived from the geometry nor assumed for every house. A house that owns it names it here and gets it wherever its profile is loaded; a house that says nothing renders none of it.

Recognised names:
  acoustic-panels — vertical oak slat panelling (Acupanel Contemporary spec) on the room-facing faces of walls 1/3 and the far face of wall 25, where those walls exist.

A house lacking the wall ids a decoration needs degrades quietly to nothing, and an unrecognised name is ignored rather than rejected, so a profile written for a newer engine still loads on an older one.

items.description: A profile-relative path to a .js file inside this house's own directory, e.g. "overlays/proposed-layout.js". Same path rule as textures: no leading slash, no '..', no absolute URL. An entry that breaks the rule is dropped with a console warning rather than failing the load.

extraOverlays.description:
OPTIONAL extra overlay scripts this profile ships next to its geometry, loaded by the page after the engine and the house are ready.

Unlike `decor` — which names geometry THIS ENGINE builds, from a closed enum — an entry here points at a script the engine does not contain and cannot validate beyond its path. The mechanism is generic; what it loads is the profile author's own code.

WHY IT LIVES IN THE PROFILE: an overlay of this kind draws something true about one particular house (a renovation plan for that building, a survey annotation), so a house that owns such a drawing should carry it wherever its profile is loaded, rather than the embedding page having to know. This is the argument `decor` already makes for panelling.

PRIVACY: this is the supported way to keep house-specific drawings OUT of a public repository. A private profile directory can hold its own overlay script and geometry together, mounted next to a public engine that ships neither.

SECURITY: a script named here runs with the page's full privileges. The path guard confines it to the profile directory so a profile cannot point the engine at an arbitrary host, but the profile directory itself must be trusted exactly as much as the page is. Do not load a profile you would not run code from.

Absent for most houses, including the demo. A profile without the field loads exactly as before.

name.description: The button label shown in Settings, e.g. "BathroomSpec".

path.description: A profile-relative path to an .html file inside this house's own directory, e.g. "specs/BathroomSpec.html". Same path rule as textures and overlays: no leading slash, no '..', no absolute URL. An entry that breaks the rule is dropped with a console warning rather than failing the load.

group.description: OPTIONAL section heading this spec button renders under in the Settings panel, e.g. "Home fittings". Purely presentational: the page recognises four department headings (Doors & Windows, Home fittings, Furniture, Decor & accessories -- a room spec such as a bathroom belongs under Home fittings) and buckets anything absent or unrecognised into an "Other" section, so a typo here can never hide a spec page — it just lands in the wrong bucket.

specPages.description:
OPTIONAL spec pages this profile ships next to its geometry. Each becomes a button in the Settings panel, appended AFTER the engine's own built-in spec list, and opens in a new tab.

A spec page is a static document describing how one particular fitting in one particular house is built — a bathroom's tiling and fixtures, an en-suite's layout. That makes it house data, not engine data, which is why it belongs here rather than in the engine's own specs/ directory.

PRIVACY: this is the supported way to keep house-specific documents OUT of a public repository, exactly as `extraOverlays` is for scripts. A private profile directory holds its spec pages next to its geometry, mounted beside a public engine that ships neither.

Unlike `extraOverlays`, nothing here is executed in the page's origin — a spec page is opened as an ordinary link — so the trust required is lower, though the path guard is the same.

Absent for most houses, including the demo. A profile without the field loads exactly as before.

site.description:
Where the house is, for the daylight rig ONLY. The engine derives sunrise/sunset and sun angle from latitude and the day of year, so the model lights up and goes dark in step with the real day.

PRIVACY: this is the one field in geometry.json that can locate a building. Give a city-level latitude, not a rooftop one — the sun rig cannot tell the difference, and a shared profile then carries no address. Omit the block entirely for a fixed neutral daylight.

latitude.description: Degrees north. City-level precision is enough and is what you should publish.

longitude.description: Degrees east. Used to offset solar noon from 12:00 UTC. Omit if the house is near the prime meridian.

locationLabel.description: Free-text label, e.g. "London, UK". Keep it as vague as the latitude.

northOffsetDegrees.description: Rotation from plan-north to true north, in degrees clockwise. A plan is rarely drawn with its top facing true north; without this the sun comes through the wrong windows. 0 means plan +y (south in plan terms) really is south.

rooms.description: Every room in the house. Order is not significant.

walls.description: The wall set. Exterior and interior walls live in the SAME list, distinguished by each wall's `exterior` flag — see the note on `wall`.

highestIdEverAssigned.description: The largest wall `id` that has ever existed in this profile, including ids since retired. Mint every new wall above this number and bump it. Without this record, a deleted wall's id gets recycled and every human reference to 'wall N' — screenshots, notes, bug reports — silently points at a different wall.

slabs.title: Floor and ceiling slabs — the two continuous horizontal surfaces
slabs.description:
OPTIONAL hand-traced outlines for the ONE floor slab and the ONE ceiling slab.

The house has exactly one floor and exactly one ceiling, each a real solid of `thickness` centimetres, and each is built as a SINGLE closed ring. They are deliberately NOT the same outline:

  floor   — traced to the INNER (room-facing) faces of the exterior walls. The floor spans the room interior only; the exterior walls sit ON it and run down through it, so there is no seam where a wall meets the floor.
  ceiling — traced to the OUTER faces of the exterior walls (the full building envelope), so it CAPS OVER the exterior walls out to their outer edge.

WHY THIS IS AUTHORED AND NOT DERIVED. A profile that omits `slabs` still gets a floor and a ceiling: the engine unions every room polygon WITH every wall footprint, which fills the strip under each wall and is therefore gap-free. That derivation is correct but blunt — it stops at the outer face of the shell for both surfaces, so it cannot express the floor/ceiling asymmetry above, and its outline is the union of many rectangles rather than the single clean ring a hand-trace gives. A house that has measured its shell states the two rings here and gets exactly them.

Each polygon is an ordered ring of [x, y] plan points in the profile's unit (centimetres), in the SAME coordinate space as rooms and walls. Do not repeat the first point at the end — the ring closes implicitly. A ring must be simple (non-self-intersecting): THREE.Shape describes one ring, and a figure-of-eight triangulates into nonsense rather than failing loudly.

floor.description: The FLOOR ring, traced to the inner (room-facing) faces of the exterior walls. Everything walkable is inside it; the exterior walls stand on it.

ceiling.description: The CEILING ring, traced to the OUTER faces of the exterior walls — the full building footprint, so the ceiling caps over the shell. Normally the larger of the two rings. Omit it to let the ceiling fall back to the derived envelope while keeping an authored `floor`; the two are independent.

thickness.description: Slab depth in centimetres, used by BOTH the floor and the ceiling. The floor grows DOWNWARD from the walking surface (into the ground) and the ceiling grows UPWARD from the wall head, so this number is never visible from inside — it is what stops the model reading as paper when the camera catches a cut edge, and it is how far below zero the exterior walls must run to meet the floor's underside.

windows.description: OPTIONAL windows and balcony glazing. Each carves its opening in its wall. Added in schemaVersion 1.1.

curtains.description: OPTIONAL curtains (blackout or sheer), hung on the room face of a wall. Added in schemaVersion 1.1.

furniture.description: OPTIONAL placed furniture: free-standing (`at` + `rotation`) or wall-anchored (`wall` + `centre` + `offset`). Each `type` is built by a module named in src/furniture/registry.js. Added in schemaVersion 1.2; an older engine ignores it.

lights.description: Lighting, grouped by room. A room with no entry simply has no lights.

cameraPresets.description:
OPTIONAL per-house camera overrides, keyed by preset name ('top', 'iso', 'front', 'se', …).

WHY OPTIONAL RATHER THAN REQUIRED: the useful presets are *directions* — top-down, the four corner three-quarter views, the four elevations — and a direction is house-independent. What genuinely varies is only the framing distance, and the engine can compute that from the footprint it already derives from the walls (fit the bounding box to the field of view). So the engine ships the direction set as defaults and auto-fits the distance; a house profile that says nothing about cameras still gets ten sensible presets, which is what a stranger modelling their first house needs.

It is not purely an engine concern either, though: a long thin house wants its 'iso' angle rotated to look down its length, and a house with a courtyard may want a target that is not the footprint centre. So the profile CAN override any preset, wholly or in part — which is why this is a per-house field that defaults to empty rather than a constant in the engine.

Each entry may be a full preset or a partial one; keys absent from a partial fall back to the engine default for that name.

roomsProfile.title: rooms.json — the Home Assistant binding
roomsProfile.description:
Maps room ids and light channels onto Home Assistant entity ids, and carries the HA connection defaults.

This file is kept OUT of geometry.json on purpose. Geometry describes shapes and is safe to publish, fork and diff; this file is an inventory of the devices installed in someone's home, and the URL of their Home Assistant. Keeping them apart means a house model can be shared without also handing over the device list, and the entity map can live in runtime config (bind-mounted, env-generated, gitignored) while the geometry stays in the repo.

The access token is NOT in this file and must never be — it comes from runtime config only.

house.description: The `id` of the geometry profile these bindings belong to. Guards against pairing one house's geometry with another's entity map.

homeAssistant.description: Connection defaults. Anything here can be overridden at runtime; a public profile should leave `url`/`fallbackUrl` unset rather than committing a hostname.

enabled.description: Whether to attempt a Home Assistant connection at all. false renders the house as a static model, which is the right default for a demo profile.

url.description: Base URL of the Home Assistant instance. Prefer supplying this via runtime config: a hostname in a committed file discloses infrastructure.

fallbackUrl.description: Alternative URL tried when `url` is unreachable (e.g. a VPN hostname). Same caution applies, more so.

wsReconnectMs.description: Delay before retrying a dropped websocket.

pollIntervalMs.description: REST poll interval used when the websocket is unavailable.

rooms.description: Room id -> channel -> entity ids. The room ids MUST exist in the paired geometry profile's `rooms`, and each channel SHOULD match a `lights[].fixtures[].channel` there — a channel with entities but no fixtures switches an entity that has nothing to draw, and fixtures with no entities render as always-off. A validator should report both as warnings rather than errors, since a half-wired house is a legitimate work-in-progress state.

additionalProperties.description: Channel -> list of Home Assistant entity ids. Several entities on one channel are switched together as a group.

sensors.description: Non-light Home Assistant bindings. Kept separate from `rooms` because that map is specifically room -> LIGHT channel -> entities, joined to geometry's lights[].fixtures[].channel; these entities drive scene state that is not a light and are not subject to that join. Every key is optional: a profile binding none of them renders exactly as before.

presence.description: Room id -> the entities whose 'on' state means that room is occupied. Room ids MUST exist in the paired geometry profile's `rooms`. Several entities on one room are OR-ed: any one 'on' means occupied, which is how a room with two motion sensors should behave.

doors.description: Door id -> the contact sensor entities for that door. Door ids MUST exist in the paired geometry profile's `doors[].id` -- keyed on the door rather than on its room because a room may have several doors, and a door need not name a room at all. Several entities are OR-ed: any one 'on' (the Home Assistant convention for a door/opening binary_sensor is on = open) swings the leaf open.

curtains.description: Curtain id -> the Home Assistant cover entities that move it. Curtain ids MUST exist in the paired geometry profile's `curtains[].id` (a sheer is a curtain too). The cover's `current_position` (0 closed .. 100 open) sets the curtain's openness and, through it, how much daylight its window lets in; 'opening'/'closing' animate toward the end stop until a settled position arrives. Several entities on one curtain are averaged. Needs rooms schemaVersion 1.2.

corniceLights.description: Curtain id -> the light entities of that curtain's cornice LED strip. The curtain MUST have a lit cornice in geometry (cornice not disabled, light not false). Bind the cornice's OWN entity here, and do not also list a 'curtain cornice' strip under the room's ambient channel in geometry.lights -- that would draw and drive the same strip twice. Several entities are OR-ed. Needs rooms schemaVersion 1.2.

climate.description: Room id -> the ONE Home Assistant climate entity that drives that room's sidebar temperature row (current temperature, target temperature, and a target slider that calls climate.set_temperature). Room ids MUST exist in the paired geometry profile's `rooms`. Deliberately a single string, not a list: a room with two climate devices (say a room thermostat and a radiator valve) picks which one the row shows here, so switching is a one-value data edit. The slider's limits come from the entity's own min_temp / max_temp / target_temp_step attributes (step defaults to 0.5). A room with no entry has no temperature row. Needs rooms schemaVersion 1.3.

vacuums.description: Furniture item id -> a robot vacuum's Home Assistant binding. The item id MUST exist in the paired geometry profile's `furniture[].id` (the robot's dock): clicking that item opens the vacuum's control card (status, battery, Start / Pause / Return to dock, and a 'clean this room' button per bound segment), and the sidebar's Controls view shows the same block. Needs rooms schemaVersion 1.4.

entity.description: The `vacuum.*` entity: its state (docked, cleaning, paused, returning, idle, error) and its `status` / `error` attributes drive the card, and vacuum.start / vacuum.pause / vacuum.return_to_base are the buttons.

battery.description: Optional battery sensor (0-100). Without it the vacuum's own `battery_level` attribute is used, if it has one.

segments.description: Optional. Room id -> the integration's own room (segment) number, one 'clean this room' button each. Room ids MUST exist in the paired geometry profile's `rooms`.

segmentService.description: The service a room clean calls, with `segments: [n]` and the vacuum as target. Defaults to the Dreame integration's.
